The Agile project manager steps in to facilitate the discussion, encourages team members to listen actively, and helps them reach a consensus without imposing a solution. What role is the Agile project manager demonstrating in this situation?
Option A: Product backlog manager
Option B: Servant leader and coach
Option C: Technical decision maker
Option D: Stakeholder proxy
Feedback: By supporting collaboration without taking control, the Agile project manager exemplifies the servant leader and coaching role essential to effective Agile facilitation.

Question Text: During a team meeting, the project manager reminds the group that the success of the project depends more on how well the team collaborates than on which task management tools they use. What principle is the project manager emphasizing?
Option A: Processes drive consistent results
Option B: Tools are required for Agile compliance
Option C: Documentation enables traceability
Option D: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Feedback: By prioritizing collaboration and team dynamics, the project manager is aligning with Agile values that recognize people as the key drivers of project success.

Question Text: A product owner is meeting with the Agile team to clarify the acceptance criteria for several backlog items. They ensure the items are prioritized correctly and explain the release schedule during the planning session. What is the product owner primarily responsible for in this scenario?
Option A: Tracking team velocity and allocating tasks accordingly
Option B: Approving budget and resource usage for upcoming iterations
Option C: Managing the product backlog and ensuring shared understanding
Option D: Assigning story points and technical estimates for each user story
Feedback: By defining acceptance criteria and ensuring backlog clarity and prioritization, the product owner fulfilling their role in managing the product backlog and aligning the team's work with customer needs.

Question Text: Each morning, the development team gathers in the same location for a short meeting. Each member shares what they accomplished yesterday, what they plan to do today, and any blockers they are facing. Which Agile practice is this team using?
Option A: Sprint Planning
Option B: Daily Scrum
Option C: Sprint Retrospective
Option D: Scrum of Scrums
Feedback: The scenario clearly aligns with the Daily Scrum format, where each member provides updates and identifies blockers to support team synchronization.

Question Text: At the beginning of a new sprint, the Scrum team gathers to determine what can be accomplished and how to structure their work. The project manager encourages the team to reflect on their past capacity and organize their approach. What event is the team participating in?
Option A: Sprint retrospective
Option B: Product backlog refinement
Option C: Sprint review
Option D: Sprint planning meeting
Feedback: The sprint planning meeting aligns the team on what to accomplish and how to approach it, setting a clear foundation for the upcoming sprint.

Question Text: You're working with a newly formed Agile team tasked with building an innovative product in an emerging market. Stakeholders are unsure whether the solution truly meets customer needs. What should the team do first?
Option A: Begin building all planned features to deliver maximum value at launch
Option B: Schedule weekly meetings with stakeholders to review project progress
Option C: Develop a small product increment to test and validate market demand
Option D: Wait until full requirements are gathered before beginning development
Feedback: Developing an early product increment enables quick feedback and ensures the team is solving the right problem, aligning with the principle of experimentation and learning early.

Question Text: An Agile team is preparing to launch a new mobile app. The marketing department wants every planned feature included in the first release to make a strong impression. However, the development team is concerned about delays and risk. The Agile project manager wants to balance early delivery with stakeholder expectations. What should the Agile project manager do?
Option A: Recommend releasing a minimal viable product (MVP) with core functionality that provides immediate value
Option B: Postpone the release date to accommodate all features in a single, polished launch
Option C: Ask marketing to remove low-priority features without input from the rest of the team
Option D: Build a prototype with mocked-up screens to satisfy stakeholders while development continues
Feedback: By focusing on MVP delivery, Agile project managers ensure the team delivers usable functionality quickly while continuing to evolve the product based on real user feedback.

Question Text: A Scrum team is preparing for the next development cycle. The product owner confirms that the team will remain unchanged, and no mid-sprint adjustments will be accepted once work begins. The team sets a 3-week window to produce a potentially shippable product increment. What does this situation best describe?
Option A: Daily Scrum
Option B: Backlog grooming
Option C: Sprint
Option D: Scrum of Scrums
Feedback: The timebox, fixed team, and no mid-sprint changes clearly indicate that this scenario describes a sprint.

Question Text: During a daily standup, the project manager notices a usually energetic developer is unusually quiet, avoids eye contact, and finishes the update quickly without offering input on team issues. What should the project manager do to support the team member and maintain a healthy team environment?
Option A: Wait until the next sprint review to see if performance changes
Option B: Publicly ask the developer during the meeting to elaborate on their update
Option C: Privately check in with the developer to better understand any unspoken concerns
Option D: Escalate the observation to HR to assess potential personal issues
Feedback: By privately addressing the issue with empathy and attention to non-verbal cues, the project manager supports team well-being and proactively nurtures a collaborative team environment.

Question Text: During a sprint review, stakeholders express concern that a critical feature demonstrated by the team is not aligned with their expectations. The feature works, but it does not address the business need they originally described. What should the project manager do to ensure future deliverables better align with stakeholder expectations?
Option A: Facilitate more frequent and collaborative backlog refinement sessions with stakeholders
Option B: Ask the stakeholders to clarify their expectations in writing before the next sprint
Option C: Instruct the team to add more documentation and user stories to clarify deliverables
Option D: Limit stakeholder involvement until after product increments are fully developed
Feedback: Facilitating regular and collaborative backlog refinement keeps stakeholders involved, ensures that priorities are continuously adjusted to match business needs, and prevents future misalignment.

Question Text: An agile project team has been receiving inconsistent feedback from stakeholders, leading to misunderstandings about what features should be included and when they are considered complete. What should the project manager do to align the team and stakeholders around a common understanding?
Option A: Create a communication management plan to regulate stakeholder input
Option B: Establish a shared vision using tools like agile modeling, personas, and the definition of "done"
Option C: Extend the iteration length to allow more time for clarification
Option D: Allow each team member to interpret stakeholder needs independently and report back weekly
Feedback: Using collaborative tools to establish a shared vision ensures consistent expectations across the team and stakeholders, reducing misunderstandings and driving project alignment.

Question Text: An Agile project manager notices that team members hesitate to suggest new approaches during retrospectives. The manager wants to foster a more creative and committed team environment. What should the project manager do first?
Option A: Establish a safe environment for experimentation and disagreement
Option B: Begin tracking all suggested improvements on a visible backlog
Option C: Assign each team member a turn to propose a new idea in each retrospective
Option D: Organize mandatory brainstorming sessions during every sprint review
Feedback: Creating a safe space for disagreement and experimentation empowers Agile teams to explore new ideas, deepen engagement, and improve continuously through trust and collaboration.

Question Text: During a sprint review, a stakeholder asks why the team is seeking feedback on a partially completed product. How should the project manager explain the purpose of this feedback?
Option A: To verify completion of the sprint backlog and formally close the sprint
Option B: To gather input before the full product is built, using completed increments to refine direction
Option C: To validate the business case before continuing development of remaining backlog items
Option D: To demonstrate the team's productivity and ensure no backlog items are missed
Feedback: Gathering feedback on completed increments ensures Agile teams stay responsive, align work with stakeholder expectations, and continuously improve through adaptive planning.

Question Text: A business representative working with an Extreme Programming (XP) team is actively involved in defining requirements, prioritizing features, and ensuring the project delivers business value. What role does this person fulfill in the XP methodology?
Option A: Coach
Option B: Tester
Option C: Programmer
Option D: Customer
Feedback: The customer role in XP is critical to steering the project by setting priorities and clarifying requirements, ensuring the product delivers the right value.

Question Text: A new team member asks for clarification on the primary artifacts used in Scrum. What should the project manager explain as the key artifacts the team uses to plan, track, and deliver work during the sprint?
Option A: Burnup chart, working agreement, and scope statement
Option B: Release plan, team charter, and status report
Option C: Product backlog, sprint backlog, and product increment
Option D: Lessons learned register, requirements traceability matrix, and quality report
Feedback: The product backlog, sprint backlog, and product increment are the core Scrum artifacts that structure planning, execution, and delivery within each sprint.

Question Text: During a project kickoff, the team realizes that strict adherence to a single Agile methodology will not meet the stakeholder's expectations due to compliance and documentation needs. They decide to integrate Agile delivery with traditional project controls to satisfy both flexibility and oversight. What Agile concept is the team applying?
Option A: Retrospective feedback
Option B: Servant leadership
Option C: Agile modeling
Option D: Process tailoring
Feedback: The team is using process tailoring to adjust their delivery approach and balance Agile flexibility with compliance needs.

Question Text: A team is using an Agile method that emphasizes software development best practices, such as continuous feedback, simplicity, and frequent code delivery. The project manager supports work prioritization, but the development team focuses heavily on technical practices like test-driven development and pair programming. Which Agile method is the team using?
Option A: Extreme Programming (XP)
Option B: Lean Software Development
Option C: Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe)
Option D: Kanban
Feedback: The team's focus on technical practices and frequent delivery aligns with Extreme Programming, which is centered around engineering excellence in Agile development.

Question Text: A team is about to begin a complex, high-risk project. To proactively prepare for challenges, the project manager organizes a meeting where the team imagines the project has failed, discusses potential causes, and identifies actions that could prevent those failures. What practice is the team applying?
Option A: Root cause analysis
Option B: Lessons learned session
Option C: Risk-adjusted backlog planning
Option D: Pre-mortem analysis
Feedback: By conducting a pre-mortem analysis, the team anticipates potential failures and integrates preventive measures before execution begins.
